---
title: "Integrations"
description: >
  Use Panache with GitHub Actions, pre-commit hooks, and dprint to format and
  lint your documents.
---

Use Panache in CI, Git hooks, and other formatting tools. For editor setup,
including RStudio, Mason, and Conform, see [Editor
Setup](lsp.qmd#editor-configuration).

## GitHub Actions

Use [panache-action](https://github.com/jolars/panache-action) to check
formatting and lint documents in CI. It installs a prebuilt Panache binary on
GitHub-hosted Linux, macOS, and Windows runners. Create
`.github/workflows/panache.yml`:

```yaml
name: Panache

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  panache:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: jolars/panache-action@v1
        with:
          version: v3.14.0
```

By default, the action checks formatting and runs the linter over the
repository's supported documents without changing files. Formatting differences
or lint findings fail the check. It uses the CLI's [configuration
discovery](../reference/configuration.qmd) and [file
selection](../reference/configuration.qmd#file-selection-directory-traversal),
including `.gitignore` and configured exclusions. Install any external
formatters or linters selected in `panache.toml` before running the action.

The `@v1` tag selects the action version; `version` selects the Panache CLI
release. Keep the latter aligned with your local installation and pre-commit
revision. Omitting `version` selects `latest`.

For a formatting-only check under `docs/`:

```yaml
- uses: jolars/panache-action@v1
  with:
    version: v3.14.0
    path: docs/
    lint: "false"
```

Set `format: "false"` to run only linting, or `config: path/to/panache.toml` to
select a configuration file. See the [action
reference](https://github.com/jolars/panache-action/tree/v1#inputs) for the
inputs and outputs supported by `@v1`.

The published `@v1` action invokes `panache format --check` and
`panache lint --check`. The latter flag is a deprecated compatibility alias;
when writing your own CI commands, use `panache lint .`.

### Manual setup (advanced)

You can also install through Cargo and invoke the checks yourself:

```yaml
name: Panache

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  panache:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - name: Install Panache
        run: cargo install --locked panache --version 3.14.0
      - name: Check formatting
        run: panache format --check .
      - name: Run linter
        run: panache lint .
```

## pre-commit

[panache-pre-commit](https://github.com/jolars/panache-pre-commit) runs Panache
on staged documents. The hooks install a prebuilt binary wheel from PyPI, so no
separate Panache or Rust installation is needed. Any configured external tools
must be installed separately and available on `PATH`.

[Install pre-commit](https://pre-commit.com/#installation), then add this entry
to `.pre-commit-config.yaml`:

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/jolars/panache-pre-commit
    rev: v3.14.0
    hooks:
      - id: panache-lint
      - id: panache-format
```

Install the Git hook and run it once over all tracked files:

```bash
pre-commit install
pre-commit run --all-files
```

On subsequent commits, both hooks select staged `.qmd`, `.Rmd`, `.md`,
`.markdown`, `.mdown`, and `.mkd` files. `panache-lint` reports findings, and
`panache-format` formats files in place. When a hook changes a file, review and
stage the changes, then commit again.

To apply safe lint fixes, add `--fix` to the lint hook and keep it before
formatting:

```yaml
hooks:
  - id: panache-lint
    args: [--fix]
  - id: panache-format
```

To check formatting without changing files, add `args: [--check]` to
`panache-format`.

Both hooks pass `--force-exclude`, so configured exclusions apply even though
pre-commit supplies filenames explicitly. They discover `panache.toml` as the
CLI does. To select another config, add `args: [--config, custom-config.toml]`
to each hook.

### File Patterns

The hook patterns are case-sensitive. For example, they do not select `.rmd`,
`.Rmarkdown`, or `.rmarkdown` by default, although Panache supports those files.
Override `files` on both hooks to cover them:

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/jolars/panache-pre-commit
    rev: v3.14.0
    hooks:
      - id: panache-lint
        files: '\.(qmd|md|markdown|mdown|mkd|[Rr]md|[Rr]markdown)$'
      - id: panache-format
        files: '\.(qmd|md|markdown|mdown|mkd|[Rr]md|[Rr]markdown)$'
```

The `rev` selects the Panache release: `v3.14.0` installs Panache 3.14.0. Run
`pre-commit autoupdate` to update hook revisions, then review and commit the
changes to `.pre-commit-config.yaml`.

## dprint

Format Markdown and Quarto documents alongside other languages with
[dprint](https://dprint.dev/) and the [Panache dprint
plugin](https://github.com/jolars/dprint-plugin-panache). The plugin bundles
Panache's formatter as WebAssembly, so no Panache CLI installation is needed.

[Install dprint](https://dprint.dev/install/). If your project has no
`dprint.json`, create one with `dprint init`, then add Panache:

```bash
dprint config add jolars/panache
```

Commit the versioned, checksummed plugin URL that the command adds to
`dprint.json`. Run `dprint fmt` to format files in place or `dprint check` to
check without changing files. The check fails when files need formatting. Both
commands run all configured plugins; Panache handles `.md`, `.qmd`, `.Rmd`,
`.rmd`, `.Rmarkdown`, `.rmarkdown`, `.markdown`, `.mdown`, and `.mkd` files.

Add settings under `panache`, keeping the `plugins` array created above:

```json
{
  "panache": {
    "wrap": "sentence",
    "lineWidth": 88
  }
}
```

The plugin uses Quarto rules for `.qmd` files and R Markdown rules for `.rmd`
and `.rmarkdown` files, regardless of the configured `flavor`. Other extensions
use `flavor`, which defaults to `pandoc`.

The plugin accepts these settings under `panache`:

  | Key                  | Values                                                                | Default     |
  | -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
  | `flavor`             | `pandoc`, `quarto`, `rmarkdown`, `gfm`, `commonmark`, `multimarkdown` | `pandoc`    |
  | `wrap`               | `reflow`, `preserve`, `sentence`, `semantic`                          | `reflow`    |
  | `blankLines`         | `collapse`, `preserve`                                                | `collapse`  |
  | `mathIndent`         | Integer number of spaces                                              | `2`         |
  | `mathDelimiterStyle` | `preserve`, `dollars`, `backslash`                                    | `preserve`  |
  | `tabStops`           | `normalize`, `preserve`                                               | `normalize` |
  | `lineEnding`         | `auto`, `lf`, `crlf`                                                  | `auto`      |
  | `lineWidth`          | Integer; uses dprint's global `lineWidth` when set                    | `80`        |
  | `tabWidth`           | Integer; uses dprint's global `indentWidth` when set                  | `4`         |

The plugin reads `dprint.json` and does not load `panache.toml`. Use dprint's
top-level `includes` and `excludes` for file selection; Panache's TOML
exclusions do not apply. dprint also respects `.gitignore`. See [dprint's
configuration guide](https://dprint.dev/config/).

The plugin provides document formatting and cannot launch Panache's external
formatters or linters. Use the CLI integrations above when code blocks need
external tools or you need lint checks.

The plugin is released independently of the CLI. Run `dprint config update`,
then review and commit the configuration changes. Matching CLI output requires
the same `panache-formatter` version and equivalent settings, with external
formatting disabled on the CLI side.
